reader.requirement: At 1985 a nested IF in statement-1 or statement-2 is matched left to right: each ELSE goes to the nearest preceding IF neither already matched with an ELSE nor implicitly/explicitly terminated, and each END-IF to the nearest preceding IF not yet terminated, including when the IF bodies hold conditional statements (ADD ON SIZE ERROR) that an ELSE or END-IF implicitly terminates and when NEXT SENTENCE is a body.

edition-consulted.switches: which [NOT] phrases a conditional statement inside the IF body may take at the target edition (ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable); it does not decide ELSE or END-IF matching

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect in ControlFlowBinder.cs#BindIf, ConditionalPhrases.cs, ProcedureFormatPass.cs; the ifStatement rule `IF condition THEN? statementBlock (ELSE statementBlock)? END_IF?` carries no edition predicate, and ELSE/END-IF matching is ANTLR's greedy nearest-IF choice, edition-blind.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: only the COBOL0903 archaic warning on NEXT SENTENCE at 2023; the matching is the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover dangling ELSE, END-IF before ELSE and phrase association; three-deep nesting, NEXT SENTENCE inside a nested IF and END-IF implicitly terminating a conditional ADD were added by the probes

probes.printed: T1-NB T2-B-TAIL T2-A-TAIL T3-ELSE T3B-SE T4-SE T4-AFTER T5-NB T5-ELSE-TAIL T5-AFTER T6-NEXT T7-NA T7-AFTER; EXPECT: MATCH (also MATCH at --std 2023)
probes.expected: each ELSE with the nearest unmatched, unterminated IF; each END-IF with the nearest unterminated IF (GR3)

probes.printed: error COBOL2269: unexpected 'ELSE'. The IF statement ends before this token
probes.expected: a second ELSE with no unmatched IF has nothing to match: refused

probes.printed: error COBOL0306: unexpected 'END-IF'. END-IF appears without a matching IF statement.
probes.expected: an END-IF with no unterminated IF: refused
an IF terminated by the separator period cannot take a later ELSE: refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.16.4 GR3  (6.16.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: The grammar's greedy optional ELSE and END_IF give the nearest-IF matching the amended GR3 states, and the binder splits the blocks at the ELSE token. The parse is edition-blind; classes a, d, e, f do not apply to a nesting rule.

refuter.evidence: rif1.cob at --std 85 (refute-1985-108/rif1-001), every line as GR3 matches: R1 NOT ON SIZE ERROR then ELSE (ELSE ends the ADD, goes to the IF) R1-NSE / R1B-E; R2 conditional ADD inside the inner IF, first ELSE to the inner IF, second to the outer: R2-NB, R2B-SE, R2C-NA; R3 inner IF ELSE then END-IF with an outer tail: R3-Y R3-TAIL R3-AFTER; R4 ELSE NEXT SENTENCE in the inner IF: R4-AFTER / R4B-NA; R5 four deep with END-IF and ELSE mixed: R5-NC R5-BT; R6 an imperative series stays in the inner ELSE: R6-Y R6-Z / R6B-NA R6B-NA2; R7 END-IF then the outer ELSE: R7-AFTER. Read 6.16.3 SR1 and 6.4.3 Scope of Statements (the next phrase of the containing statement ends an unterminated contained one): matches. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.16.4 GR3 (reader's line).
